| $x$ | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $2$ | $-3$ | $5$ | $-2$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
question.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $2$ | $-3$ | $5$ | $-2$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & {5}^{2} \\ 1 & {6}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.
